column1: # Written by Claude (origin "claude"). One line per entry:  entry id|typical learner mistake|usage note
# Notes are in English. Either text column may be empty.
pt:ser:verb|Ser is for identity and lasting qualities ("sou brasileiro", "ela é alta"), estar for states and temporary situations ("estou cansado", "estou em casa").|
pt:estar:verb|Estar is for states and where things or people are right now ("estou cansado", "ele está em Zurique"); ser for identity and lasting qualities.|
pt:ter:verb||In Brazil ter also means "there is / there are": "tem um café aqui". More formal: "há".
pt:haver:verb||Há means "there is / there are" and also "ago": "há dois anos" (two years ago).
pt:ficar:verb||Ficar means to stay, but also to become ("fiquei triste") and to be located ("onde fica o banco?").
pt:você:pronoun||In Brazil você is the usual "you", with the verb in the third person: "você fala". In Portugal tu is common among friends and você can sound distant.
pt:gente:noun||"A gente" means "we" in everyday Brazilian Portuguese, with a singular verb: "a gente vai".
pt:puxar:verb|Puxar means to pull, even though it looks like "push". To push is empurrar.|
pt:empurrar:verb|Empurrar means to push; puxar means to pull.|
pt:pretender:verb|Pretender means to intend, not to pretend (fingir).|
pt:assistir:verb|"Assistir a" means to watch (a film, TV) or to attend. To help is ajudar.|
pt:atualmente:adverb|Means currently, not actually. "Actually" is "na verdade".|
pt:esquisito:adjective|Means strange, weird, not exquisite (requintado).|
pt:costume:noun|Costume means habit or custom. A costume is "fantasia".|
pt:parente:noun|Parente means relative (family member). Parents are "pais".|
pt:pai:noun||"Os pais" means the parents (mother and father). "País", with an accent, means country.
pt:propaganda:noun||In Brazil propaganda usually means an advertisement.
pt:legal:adjective||In Brazil legal also means cool, nice: "que legal!"
pt:fazer:verb||Faz is used for time ago and for weather: "faz dois anos", "faz frio".
pt:ir:verb||Ir + infinitive is the near future: "vou estudar".
pt:saber:verb|Saber is for facts and skills ("sei nadar"), conhecer for people and places ("conheço Lisboa").|
pt:conhecer:verb|Conhecer is for people and places; for facts and skills use saber: "sei onde ele mora".|
pt:gostar:verb|Gostar needs de: "gosto de café", "gosto de você".|
pt:obrigado:interjection|A man says obrigado, a woman obrigada.|
pt:mesmo:adverb||After a word, mesmo means really or even: "é mesmo?" (really?), "mesmo assim" (even so).
pt:pegar:verb||In Brazil you "pegar o ônibus"; in Portugal you "apanhar o autocarro".
pt:educado:adjective|Educado means polite. Educated is "instruído" or "culto".|
pt:tirar:verb||Tirar has many uses: take off (tirar o casaco), take a photo (tirar uma foto), get a grade (tirar dez).
